title: Prefetch-backpressure Playbook and Weekly Sync
summary: Weekly sync: capture operational playbook for request prefetch + backpressure interactions with KV cache and micro-batching. Goal is a pragmatic list of heuristics, short-term experiments, and an escalation ladder for oncall teams.
body:
Context:
This doc consolidates what we learned running the 2028-08 prefetch canary across eu-west and us-west clusters. We observed two recurring failure modes: 1) prefetch floods filling KV cache causing eviction storms and miss amplification, 2) prefetch-induced micro-batching that increases p95 latency under tail-load. The playbook below is intended to guide engineers and oncall through detection, mitigation, and experiments to minimize regressions while preserving hit-rate and cost wins from prefetching.

High-level goals:
- Preserve tail latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms steady-state for hosted-critical routes.
- Keep KV cache hit rate >= 78% for conversational workloads with median ctx=512.
- Avoid allocator thrash / OOMs on prefetched shards.
- Provide deterministic backpressure path that degrades gracefully (fall back to conservative batching or synchronous fetch).

Observations from canary (eu-west, 2028-08-22 -> 2028-08-29):
- Aggregate token throughput increased ~9% with prefetch-on-heavy.
- KV cache global hit rate rose from 68% -> 75% during steady periods but dipped to 53% during bursty arrivals (spikes of concurrent sessions > 4k).
- p50 unchanged, p95 increased 18ms on average; p99 had 45ms spikes correlated with concurrent evictions and micro-batch formation.
- GPU utilization improved slightly (~3%) in steady state; memory pressure on workers rose 12% and triggered GC/eviction cycles.

Root cause hypotheses:
- Prefetch pipeline incorrectly piggybacks on optimistic session joins, causing simultaneous prefetches for many sessions that touch different KV shards -> eviction storm.
- Batching heuristic groups prefetched inflight requests into micro-batches that exceed the latency budget when queueing overlap occurs.
- Cache admission policy lacks a TTL-aware admission weight for prefetched entries.

Playbook (operational steps)
1) Detection (oncall):
   - Dashboard checks (run immediately):
     - p95 token latency per route (alert if > 120ms for 5m).
     - KV cache miss rate (alert if miss_rate > 40% and trending up in 5m).
     - Eviction rate spikes (alert if evictions/min > baseline * 4).
     - Worker RSS / mem pressure alerts.
   - Quick triage commands:
     - curl -s https://ops.internal/api/metrics?route=<route>&window=5m | jq '.metrics["kv_evictions_per_min"]'
     - grafana link: perf/serving/runtime/prefetch-backpressure

2) Immediate mitigations (hotfix style):
   - If eviction storm + p95 spike: toggle prefetch -> conservative via runtime flag:
     - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/flags -d '{"prefetch_mode":"conservative"}'
     - conservative = disables speculative prefetch for sessions with concurrency>8, limits concurrent prefetches per worker to 32.
   - If micro-batching queueing is the culprit: reduce batching window to 6ms on affected SKUs:
     - config snippet: BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=6
   - If memory pressure remains high: reduce per-worker prefetch queue depth: prefetch_depth=8 -> 4.

3) Short-term fixes to deploy in next patch (priority A):
   - Add TTL-weighted admission: prefer admitting prefetched entries with predicted reuse probability > 0.15, otherwise insert as cold miss-protected small-ttl entries. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2839)
   - Prefetch jittering: stagger prefetch start times across sessions using a fast deterministic jitter (0-12ms) to avoid synchronous storms.
   - Backpressure token: track per-shard inflight prefetch counter; if > threshold, reject new prefetch with 503->client side fallback to sync fetch.

4) Medium-term experiments (A/B in dedicated capacity):
   - Experiment 1: Admission policy with size-aware weight vs TTL-only. Metric: net cost per 10k tokens and hit-rate delta over 24h.
   - Experiment 2: Prefetch sampling at 50% for long-tail routes to measure trade-off for recall vs cache pollution.
   - Experiment 3: Micro-batch window auto-tuner: adapt window by measuring micro-batch queueing latency; goal reduce p95 by 10% without >3% throughput loss.

5) Escalation ladder (who to page):
   - Oncall SRE first: if p95 > 250ms or evictions/min > baseline*6 -> page eng-serving-runtime leads: Marcus Reed, Evelyn Park.
   - If memory OOMs observed or persistent degradation after mitigations -> page infra platform-eng: Priya Nair.

Experiment results snapshot (canary summary):
- Prefetch jittering dry-run (canary group ~1200 qps): reduced coincident prefetch starts by 72%, reduced eviction spikes by 40%, p95 improved 9ms.
- Conservative mode toggled for high-concurrency sessions: tail-latency regained baseline numbers but hit rate decreased 4 pt. Cost impact: +2% token cost.

Open decisions (needs engineering signoff):
- What is acceptable hit-rate vs tail-latency trade-off for hosted-critical? Suggested: enforce p95 <= 120ms as hard SLO and allow hit-rate to fluctuate within +/- 5 pts.
- Should prefetch be enabled by default for Dedicated customers? Proposed default: off; enable via feature flag per tenant.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- (Anika) Ship TTL-weighted admission initial PR with unit tests and integration test harness. ETA: 2028-09-12.
- (Marcus) Add per-shard inflight counters and expose metric kv_prefetch_inflight_per_shard. ETA: 2028-09-09.
- (Evelyn) Run micro-batch window auto-tuner prototype on dedicated staging with 24h run. ETA: 2028-09-16.
- (Diego) Create dashboard panels for prefetch jitter overlap % and correlate with eviction spikes. ETA: 2028-09-08.
- (Priya) Define failure SLA for prefetch toggle rollback and add to runbook. ETA: 2028-09-10.

Meeting notes (2028-09-05 weekly sync):
Attendees: Anika, Marcus, Evelyn, Diego, Priya, SRE oncall (Jamal).
Highlights:
- Jamal: observed two customer incidents; both resolved by toggling conservative prefetch flag.
- Marcus: merged lightweight probe to measure per-shard inflight prefetch (hotfix deployed to staging).
- Evelyn: proposed auto-tuner algorithm; need synthetic trace that reproduces bursty session start pattern.
- Diego: suggested adding admission sampling for prefetched entries below reuse threshold.
- Decision: proceed with TTL-weighting PR and schedule A/B experiments targeting 10% of traffic in us-west.

Retention / attachments:
- Attach test logs: s3://redwood-test-logs/prefetch/canary-2028-08-22-29 (pointer)
- Raw bench results: ./attachments/prefetch-canary-raw.csv (on eng shared bucket)

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- Add short checklist for oncall runbook: how to toggle flags, how to query prefetch inflight, safe rollback steps.
- Draft confluence page from this doc and link to PRs/graphs.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Check per-shard inflight: curl -s https://ops.internal/api/shards/prefetch_inflight | jq '.shards | sort_by(.inflight) | reverse | .[:10]'
- Toggle conservative prefetch mode: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/flags -d '{"prefetch_mode":"conservative","note":"oncall rollback"}'
- Batching window change (k8s env var): kubectl set env deploy/runtime-worker BATCHING_WINDOW_MS=6 -n serving-runtime

End of sync.
decisions: Enable conservative prefetch default for sessions with concurrency > 8
Require p95 <= 120ms as hard SLO for hosted-critical routes
Run A/B experiments for TTL-weighted admission and micro-batch auto-tuner
